label: L2M v1
lesson: The early narrative connects production constraints to four recurring customer needs: scale, affordability, consistent quality, and industrial volume. It also distinguishes material sales from licensing and advisory.

label: L2M v2
lesson: The thermal-management exploration adds an application-specific question: can 2D-filled polymer composites meet the performance and qualification requirements of a prospective industrial user? This is an exploratory branch, rather than an established customer win.

label: L2M v3
lesson: This draft tests concrete and composites additives as a beachhead and graphite/mining as a strategic second route. A proposed six-month plan links interviews, a pilot partner, samples, benchmarks, and IP planning.

label: L2M v4
lesson: The partnership and scale-up material connects industry-relevant graphite and application requirements to pilot validation, IP protection, and a proposed $2.5M industrial scale-up plan.

label: L2M v5
lesson: The material story moves from graphene and battery potential to the production bottleneck, a CFE process concept, industrial validation, and automation. Application benefits explain the opportunity; they are not presented here as measured product results.

label: L2M v6
lesson: The TAM, SAM, and SOM framing adds a broader view of the platform opportunity alongside pilot and investment planning. These market estimates remain contextual pitch assumptions, separate from the discovery-led entry-market choices.

label: Final presentation
lesson: The final deck reports 40+ interviews, identifies graphite/mining and concrete as two entry markets, and makes continued discovery, pilot connections, assumption testing, and starting the IP process the next steps.
